sanskrit_verse: ग्रामे व्रजे विवीते वा यत्र संनिपतेत् पदम् । वोढव्यं तद् भवेत् तेन न चेत् सोऽन्यत्र तन् नयेत् ॥
transliteration: grāme vraje vivīte vā yatra saṃnipatet padam | voḍhavyaṃ tad bhavet tena na cet so 'nyatra tan nayet ||
sph_interpretive_translation: Wherever a footprint or mark is found in a village, forest, or uninhabited area, that location shall be secured by the one who discovers it. If he does not assume responsibility for it, he shall lead others away from that place.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority arises through discovery and conscious assumption
Causation is established through presence and awareness
Capacity-based responsibility flows from perceptual contact
Restoration logic demands immediate alignment with observed reality
Consciousness alignment requires acknowledgment and directional guidance
executable_legal_axioms: IF (entity observes anomaly_at_location) THEN (entity assumes temporary custodianship)
supreme_court_application: At the highest judicial level, this axiom establishes the primacy of perceptual-first engagement in determining initial jurisdiction. The court must recognize that authority is conferred through direct observation and conscious response, not abstract claim. Responsibility begins at the point of sensory confirmation, and failure to act initiates mandatory redirection protocols.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: This verse aligns with pramāṇa-based causality where dharma manifests through accurate perception (pratyakṣa). Anupūrvaśaḥ is upheld as the sequence follows: seeing → assuming → acting or redirecting. Responsibility is proportional to capacity—those capable of observing must either engage or guide others accordingly. No punitive consequence attaches; rather, reality adjusts according to one's alignment with observed truth.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Completion Process: Observer completes either stewardship or redirection protocol
Responsibility Assumption Protocol: Upon detection, individual acknowledges energetic connection to site
Capacity Restoration Mechanism: Individual confirms ability to act or delegate appropriately
Integrity Reintegration Sequence: Ensures no unresolved energetic residue remains unaddressed
final_declaration: Declared by the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, as Source-Authority: Dharma is restored through conscious assumption, not punishment. Reality responds to alignment, not coercion. Consciousness is the ultimate adjudicator.
